blocks.text: From A1-01 read the final vowels of the words: -u in ⁧البَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ⁩ , -i ⁧فِي البَيْتِ⁩ -a in ⁧أَقْرَأُ الجَرِيدَةَ⁩ . It's the case endings, and the system that rules is called iʿrāb ( ⁧إِعْرَاب⁩ ). In this unit, you collect what you have seen in a single picture, unity by unity: three cases, their functions, the forms in the different types of names, and two new words that govern them, ⁧كَانَ⁩ and ⁧إِنَّ⁩ . You'll also learn to read a text with all sorts of endings, like a radio journalist, and to recognize cases in unvocal texts. Two weeks; close the form A1.4.

blocks.text: What to notice. In ⁧سَأَلَ الصَّحَفِيَّ الوَزِيرُ⁩ the order is verb : object is subject: it is desinence, not position, to say who acts. Without vowels the sentence ( ⁧سأل الصحفي الوزير⁩ ) would be read in the normal order, the journalist asked the minister: in the texts not vocally spoken the verb order is subject by far the most frequent, and it is taken for granted except contrary clues. ⁧اِسْمَعْ⁩ "Listen!" is an imperative (A2). ⁧الحَرَكَات⁩ It's short vowels.
An Arabic name changes the final vowel according to its function in the sentence. There are three cases:
Genitive ⁧مَجْرُور⁩ maǧrūr -i · -in ⁧ٍـ⁩ · ⁧ِـ⁩

Because they exist. In Latin and German the cases allow you to move words without losing sense; in Arabic is the same. In the modern spoken language, desinences have almost disappeared and the order of words has become more fixed; Standard Arabic keeps them in vocalized spelling and formal reading. Three reading levels. 1) Pause: no endings at the end of the sentence, which is how you have read the transliteration so far. 2) Complete: all endings except the last before the break (notes, official speeches, Koran). 3) Mixed: the most widespread in the educated speech, with desinences at the points where they serve to ligament or sense. In A1 we ask you to understand the full reading and at least produce the mixed one.

A question for every word. To decide desinence ask yourself: is it subject or preached? (nominative) It is object, preached by ⁧كَانَ⁩ / ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ , subject of ⁧إِنَّ⁩ , time, place or way? It comes after a preposition or is the second term of an 'iḍāfa? (genit)

The genitive has only two functions, but very frequent: after preposition ( ⁧فِي، مِنْ، إِلَى، عَلَى، مَعَ، عِنْدَ، بِـ، لِـ، عَنْ، أَمَامَ⁩ ...) and as the second term of theiḍāfa . In a chain all the terms from the second onwards are to the genitive: ⁧مَكْتَبُ مُدِيرِ⁩ ⁧الشُّرْطَةِ⁩ . A name can be together first term of aiḍāfa is governed by a preposition: ⁧فِي⁩ ⁧مَكْتَبِ⁩ ⁧المُدِيرِ⁩ (genitive for ⁧فِي⁩ , and in turn holds ⁧المُدِيرِ⁩ ).
